MI.snippet: A record search and copies must be furnished without charge for the first $20 of the fee for each request by a qualifying indigent individual (with affidavit) or by a state-designated developmental-disabilities/mental-il

MO.snippet: A public body may waive or reduce the fees when it determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.

NE.snippet: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee if the waiver or reduction would be in the public interest.

NV.snippet: A governmental entity may waive all or part of a copy fee if it adopts a written waiver policy and posts a legible sign or notice of the policy's terms at each office providing copies.

OK.snippet: No search fee may be charged when release of the records is in the public interest, including release to news media, scholars, authors, and taxpayers seeking to determine whether officials are performing their duties.

OR.snippet: The custodian may furnish copies without charge or at a substantially reduced fee if it determines the waiver or reduction is in the public interest because making the record available primarily benefits the general publ

PA.snippet: An agency may waive duplication fees, including when the requester duplicates the record or when the agency deems it in the public interest to do so.

SC.snippet: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if documents are subject to disclosure.

citations: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.D
TN.snippet: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.

TX.snippet: The body must provide a copy without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest because providing the copy primarily benefits the general public.

UT.snippet: An entity may (and is encouraged to) fulfill a request without charge if release primarily benefits the public, the requester is the subject of/specified in the record, or the requester's legal rights are directly implic

VA.snippet: The reasonable-charge fee provisions do not apply to scholastic records that must be made available under FERPA when requested by a parent or legal guardian of a minor student or by a student who is 18 or older.

WA.snippet: If the requester fails to inspect, pay for, or claim an installment of a records request, the agency need not fulfill the balance of the request.

WI.snippet: An authority may provide copies without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest.

citations: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.C
OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.D
OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.A
TN.snippet: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.
